gloss: good catch; bumper haul; abundant fishing

definitions.gloss: good catch; bumper haul; abundant fishing
definitions.explanation: An especially large or plentiful fish catch. Used for both a single outing's results and a season's overall yield.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{豊漁|ほうりょう}だ。
examples.english: It's a good catch this year.

examples.japanese: サンマが{豊漁|ほうりょう}で{値段|ねだん}が{下|さ}がった。
examples.english: Saury prices dropped because of the abundant catch.

examples.japanese: {漁師|りょうし}たちは{豊漁|ほうりょう}を{祈|いの}って{出港|しゅっこう}した。
examples.english: The fishermen set out to sea praying for a bountiful catch.

notes:
A compound of {豊|ほう} (abundant, rich) and {漁|りょう} (fishing, catch). The antonym is {不漁|ふりょう} (poor catch). Commonly seen in seasonal news reports about fish catches.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {豊漁|ほうりょう}に{恵|めぐ}まれる: to be blessed with a good catch
- {豊漁|ほうりょう}を{祈|いの}る: to pray for an abundant catch
- {記録的|きろくてき}な{豊漁|ほうりょう}: a record-breaking catch
- {豊漁|ほうりょう}{貧乏|びんぼう}: poverty due to an oversupply of fish (prices crash so fishermen lose money despite catching more)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大漁|たいりょう}: big catch — more casual and celebratory; often seen on fishing flags ({大漁旗|たいりょうばた})
- {不漁|ふりょう}: poor catch — the antonym
- {豊作|ほうさく}: bumper crop — the agricultural equivalent (for farming, not fishing)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{豊漁|ほうりょう}{貧乏|びんぼう} is a well-known economic paradox in Japan: when the catch is too good, fish prices plummet and fishermen's income actually decreases despite the abundance.
